description.text:
Create various nodes from the track data,

Use CornerPin2D relative to warp the image according to the relative transform between the current frame and the reference frame.

Use CornerPin2D absolute to set the to position knobs to the corners of the planar surface, and the from knob positions to the dimensions of the currently selected node. This will place the incoming image entirely inside the planar surface.

Use CornerPin2D stabilize to apply the inverse transform of the track to stabilize the image. This locks down the image so that the tracked plane effectively doesn't move. This can be very useful for applying drift corrections.

Use Tracker to create a four-corner Tracker node with each of the trackers taking the positions of planar surface corners. This allows you to use the Tracker's transform functions to stabilize, reduce jitter, etc. This export option needs to be baked out in order for the transform to work correctly.

Each of the exports also has a "bake" option, which will copy the values of the key-frames out, instead of creating expression links.

  else: 
    p.setValue(k.getValue(0),0) 
    p.setValue(k.getValue(1),1)

lastColumn = 0

  lastColumn = currentColumn 
  while currentColumn < (lastColumn + maxColumns): 
    if tracks.fullyQualifiedName(currentColumn).find('.'+str(i+1)+'.track_x') != -1: 
      k = ptracker[inKnobs[i]] 
      tracks.setAnimated(currentColumn)

      tracks.setExpression(ptracker.name()+'.'+inKnobs[i]+'.y', currentColumn+1) 
      break

description.plain_text: PlanarTracker Track a planar surface through a sequence. The PlanarTracker is used for tracking image regions of flat or nearly flat surfaces. This node generally uses a Roto(Paint) node to specify which regions in the Source input to track. To start tracking, create a PlanarTrack layer in the Roto(Paint) curves menu if one does not already exist. (If you created the PlanarTracker node through the Nuke menu, a layer will already be set up, otherwise see below.) In this layer, start drawing the region(s) you want to track, they will show up in purple.Begin tracking by using the controls found in the Roto(Paint) node's tracking toolbar at the top of the Viewer. The toolbar will also show you which track layer is currently being tracked. As you track, the tracking data will be baked into your PlanarTrack layer in the curves panel. Any subsequent shapes added to this layer will inherit from the track transform. In the curves panel, if the icon in the "PT" column is off, the shape will not contribute to the tracking region, but will be affected by the track. To create a new track layer, draw a shape (or shapes) on the region(s) you want to track, right-click the selected shapes in the Viewer and select one of the "planar-track" options. You can also do this from the Roto curves panel. Note, you'll need to draw these shapes outside of an existing track layer. The drop-down menu on the right of the Roto(Paint) node's tracking toolbar can be used to switch between track layers, or create new ones. You can also use an existing mask to specify the region to be tracked. For example, the result of a colour key or user matte. Simply supply this to the Mask input, and select the appropriate "mask" knob in the PlanarTracker panel. This mask will then be used in addition to any shapes you have drawn in Roto.If parts of your track are not locking on correctly, you can use the drift correction controls in the tracking toolbar. More information on correction can be found in the User Guide. When you're happy with your track, you can get access to the track transform via CornerPin2D nodes found in the "Export" drop-down, either in the tracking toolbar in the Viewer, or from the PlanarTracker node's properties panel.
description.text:
PlanarTracker Track a planar surface through a sequence. The PlanarTracker is used for tracking image regions of flat or nearly flat surfaces. This node generally uses a Roto(Paint) node to specify which regions in the Source input to track. To start tracking, create a PlanarTrack layer in the Roto(Paint) curves menu if one does not already exist. (If you created the PlanarTracker node through the Nuke menu, a layer will already be set up, otherwise see below.) In this layer, start drawing the region(s) you want to track, they will show up in purple.

Begin tracking by using the controls found in the Roto(Paint) node's tracking toolbar at the top of the Viewer. The toolbar will also show you which track layer is currently being tracked. As you track, the tracking data will be baked into your PlanarTrack layer in the curves panel. Any subsequent shapes added to this layer will inherit from the track transform. In the curves panel, if the icon in the "PT" column is off, the shape will not contribute to the tracking region, but will be affected by the track.

To create a new track layer, draw a shape (or shapes) on the region(s) you want to track, right-click the selected shapes in the Viewer and select one of the "planar-track" options. You can also do this from the Roto curves panel. Note, you'll need to draw these shapes outside of an existing track layer. The drop-down menu on the right of the Roto(Paint) node's tracking toolbar can be used to switch between track layers, or create new ones.

You can also use an existing mask to specify the region to be tracked. For example, the result of a colour key or user matte. Simply supply this to the Mask input, and select the appropriate "mask" knob in the PlanarTracker panel. This mask will then be used in addition to any shapes you have drawn in Roto.

If parts of your track are not locking on correctly, you can use the drift correction controls in the tracking toolbar. More information on correction can be found in the User Guide.

When you're happy with your track, you can get access to the track transform via CornerPin2D nodes found in the "Export" drop-down, either in the tracking toolbar in the Viewer, or from the PlanarTracker node's properties panel.
